label: input token l at original positions 0-4
explanation: Token detector for the letter l in the original (pre-<DEL>) phase, limited to positions 0-4. Every l input at t<=4 activates the feature (precision 1.0 on dev). Magnitude is highest at t=0-2 (about 0.8-1.0 of max) and drops at later positions (t=3 lower, t=4 often only about 0.25 of max); it fades out at t=5 (a few weak activations) and is silent from t=6 on. Repeated l still fires (slightly weaker than the first l). Does not fire on l during the delimiter or copy phase (when the model outputs or is fed l back), nor on other tokens, apart from rare tiny activations (about 0.02 of max) on y/0 after an initial r.

issues: Small wording error: the explanation says the feature is 'silent from t=6 on', but the dev profile shows 65 tiny copy-phase activations at t=7-11 (231 copy-phase activations in total, mostly at recall_idx 2, e.g. a fed-back l at about 0.02). They carry roughly 0 activation mass, so this is noise rather than a pattern.
Test misses (2819 steps, 0.1% of mass) fall into two groups. One is l at t=5 with activations of 0.01-0.05. The other is y or 0 at t=1 after an initial r, at 0.02. Both match the explanation.
Widening the predicate to t<=5 does worse: test F1 0.937 versus 0.983, because l at t=5 is active only 13% of the time. So the t<=4 cutoff is the right boundary.

No false positives on test (precision 1.000). The magnitude claims match the per-t mass shares: the mean at t=4 is about 0.28 of the mean at t=0. A repeated l in the examples is weaker (0.56 after 0.91). I could not confirm this in bulk: an n_seen(["l"]) > 0 predicate matched 0 steps, which looks like a quirk of the helper.
